title: The Superhabit of Foresight
author: Andrew Abela
summary: Andrew Abela presents Foresight as the superhabit for setting goals, staying focused on them and updating them as conditions change, one of eight superhabits within Practical Wisdom. He cites research linking goal-setting to success, satisfaction, motivation and even health outcomes, and notes that writing goals down, sharing them and reporting progress are each associated with greater accomplishment. His advice is to focus on a small number of important goals, to choose the one thing that makes everything else easier, and to let goals rather than email set the day's priorities. Case examples include Domino's founder Tom Monaghan's written, specific, time-limited goal system and Ronald Reagan's single clear Cold War aim, against which most of his administration's actions were measured. The simple first step is to write down one goal each day.
points: Foresight means setting goals, staying focused on them and revising them as conditions change, and it is associated with greater success, motivation and satisfaction.

Tom Monaghan's system shows that specific, written, time-limited goals are easier to communicate and rally others around.
